title: When an Indian Emperor Sent a Navy Overseas
description: 1025: Rajendra Chola's naval expedition against Srivijaya.

scenes.narration: Nearly a thousand years ago, an Indian emperor sent a fleet across the Bay of Bengal.
scenes.image_prompt: fleet of large medieval Indian wooden ships with sails crossing a blue ocean

scenes.narration: It's 1025. The Chola emperor Rajendra the First rules South India from Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
scenes.image_prompt: Chola emperor in royal court with a grand granite temple behind, 11th century

scenes.narration: His target: the kingdom of Srivijaya, which controls key sea routes in Southeast Asia.
scenes.image_prompt: Southeast Asian harbour city with trading ships and palm trees, 11th century

scenes.narration: Chola ships cross the ocean to Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula.
scenes.image_prompt: Chola warships with soldiers and elephants on deck sailing toward a tropical coast

scenes.narration: Inscriptions list the places they attacked, including Kadaram, in today's Malaysia.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Tamil inscription carved on a temple wall, close up

scenes.narration: The campaign helped protect Tamil merchants trading with China and Southeast Asia.
scenes.image_prompt: Tamil merchants trading spices and textiles with Chinese traders at a busy port

scenes.narration: Chola influence spread across the ocean.
scenes.image_prompt: Chola ships in a tropical harbour at sunset, temples on shore

scenes.narration: Most people have never heard this story. Which Indian empire should we cover next?
